scope: Proposition 3.1 (Primitive addition with preserved boundary conditions) of the manuscript “Smooth isometric immersions of closed surfaces into Euclidean four-space” (preprints/Smooth-isometric-immersions-of-closed-surfaces-into-Euclidean-four-space-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 333 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1f0bf283be86c80b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let M be a closed smooth surface and F : M → R4 a smooth immersion whose second fundamental form is nonzero as a tensor at every point. Assume F has a preferred normal n. Let D be a disk with smooth boundary C0 and coordinates (x, y) on a neighborhood of D. Let a ∈ C∞(M) be nonnegative, positive exactly on D, and put Y0 = ∂y. Suppose Hessγ(F) x(∂y, ∂y) > 0 on D. (3.4) Let C1, . . . , Cm be finitely many later curves with nonzero smooth vector fields Yi on their neighbor- hoods. Assume the following: 1. All curves C0, . . . , Cm are pairwise transverse and have no triple intersection. 2. On the portion of each later curve Ci, 1 ≤ i ≤ m, in D, the vector ∂y is tangent to Ci at only finitely many points. 3. At every Ci ∩ Cl ∩ D with distinct i, l > 0, dx(Yi) ̸= 0 and dx(Yl) ̸= 0. 4. Conditions (3.3) hold for all indices 0, . . . , m. Then, for every ε > 0, there are a smooth immersion F+ : M → R4 and a preferred normal n+ such that γ(F+) = γ+ := γ(F) + a2 dx2 , BF+ ̸= 0 at every point, conditions (3.3) hold for (F+, n+) and all later indices 1, . . . , m, and ∥F+ − F∥C2(M\D) < ε. The tensor a2dx2 is extended by zero outside the coordinate neighborhood.
